questions.question: In the context of Addition Reactions of Alkenes, what is the major organic product when Propene (CH₃-CH=CH₂) reacts under the following conditions: Anhydrous HBr(g)?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Protonation yields the secondary carbocation, which is trapped by bromide to give the Markovnikov product. The correct major product is '2-Bromopropane (CH₃-CHBr-CH₃)'.

questions.question: In the context of Addition Reactions of Alkenes, what is the major organic product when Propene reacts under the following conditions: HBr / ROOR with hν?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Radical mechanism: Br• radical attacks the less substituted carbon to generate the more stable 2° radical intermediate. The correct major product is '1-Bromopropane (CH₃CH₂CH₂Br)'.

questions.question: In the context of Addition Reactions of Alkenes, what is the major organic product when 2-Methylpropene reacts under the following conditions: H₂O / cat. H₂SO₄ (50°C)?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Protonation forms a stable tertiary carbocation, captured by water to yield tert-butanol. The correct major product is '2-Methyl-2-propanol [(CH₃)₃C-OH]'.

questions.question: In the context of Addition Reactions of Alkenes, what is the major organic product when 3,3-Dimethyl-1-butene reacts under the following conditions: 1. Hg(OAc)₂, H₂O  2. NaBH₄, NaOH?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Bridged mercurinium ion prevents carbocation rearrangements, yielding the unrearranged Markovnikov alcohol. The correct major product is '3,3-Dimethyl-2-butanol (Markovnikov, no shift)'.

questions.question: In the context of Addition Reactions of Alkenes, what is the major organic product when 1-Methylcyclopentene reacts under the following conditions: 1. BH₃·THF  2. Basic H₂O₂ (NaOH)?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Concerted syn-addition of B-H places OH on the less substituted carbon with trans stereochemistry relative to methyl. The correct major product is 'trans-2-Methylcyclopentanol (Anti-Markovnikov, Syn)'.

questions.question: Which reaction conditions / reagents are required to convert 1,2-Dimethylcyclohexene into cis-1,2-Dimethylcyclohexane (Syn addition) in Addition Reactions of Alkenes?
questions.explanation: Reagent selection rationale: The transformation '1,2-Dimethylcyclohexene' → 'cis-1,2-Dimethylcyclohexane (Syn addition)' specifically requires 'H₂ / Pt(s) catalyst, 25°C'. Mechanistic basis: Both hydrogen atoms are delivered simultaneously to the same face of the alkene from the metal catalyst surface.

questions.question: Which reaction conditions / reagents are required to convert Cyclohexene into trans-1,2-Dibromocyclohexane (Anti addition) in Addition Reactions of Alkenes?
questions.explanation: Reagent selection rationale: The transformation 'Cyclohexene' → 'trans-1,2-Dibromocyclohexane (Anti addition)' specifically requires 'Br₂ / dry CH₂Cl₂'. Mechanistic basis: Backside attack of bromide on the cyclic bromonium ion enforces strictly anti stereochemistry.

questions.question: Which reaction conditions / reagents are required to convert Propene into 1-Bromo-2-propanol (Major Markovnikov/Anti) in Addition Reactions of Alkenes?
